items.title: Robinson arithmetic, PA, and numeral conventions
items.statement: Q has the universal closures of Sx≠0, Sx=Sy→x=y, x≠0→∃y x=Sy, x+0=x, x+Sy=S(x+y), x·0=0, x·Sy=x·y+x. PA adds full formula induction with parameters. Numeral n is S iterated n times on 0. Define x≤y by ∃z(z+x=y), and x<y by x≤y and x≠y.
items.strategy: List every axiom with primitive negation/conjunction/existential expansions and least-fresh-variable substitution. No induction schema belongs to Q. The order convention matters because Q does not prove addition commutative.

items.title: Effective theories and certified numerical proof codes
items.statement: Fix an effectively presented finite-arity countable signature with primitive-recursive symbol/arity tests. An effective axiom presentation is ∃w E(a,w) with primitive-recursive E, a finite computation certificate for enumeration if necessary. A proof includes an E-certificate for every nonlogical axiom occurrence. Encode each token, annotation and finite list numerically; invalid codes have specified default values. For a binary word w set c(w)=1^{|w|}0w. With bin(0)=0 and otherwise canonical binary numerals, encode (a0,...,a{k-1}) by the natural number with binary word 1 1^k 0 c(bin(a0))...c(bin(a{k-1})). The empty code is 2. Invalid numerical words have validity false and length/entries zero; out-of-range coordinates return zero. These operations, fixed-arity encoding, append and finite histories are supplied by the following local lemma.
items.strategy: The primitive-recursive class, all arities including nullary zero, parameter recursion and totality come from the published bounded-arithmetic definition, not A609. The initial 1 prevents leading-zero ambiguity. The unary length and payload lengths make parsing deterministic; the following lemma proves injectivity, primitive-recursive validity and operations. Each certified proof is a coded finite list and each nonlogical axiom carries its finite E-witness. A c.e. enumeration certificate records a finite transition history, not a decision oracle.

items.title: Primitive-recursive sentinel coding for certified syntax
items.statement: In ZF, the specified sentinel sequence coding is injective. Its validity predicate, total length and coordinate functions (zero on invalid inputs or out-of-range coordinates), append and concatenation operations, and each fixed-arity encoder are primitive recursive. Fixed finite-state numerical recursions and recursions recording their finite histories are primitive recursive. No A609, choice axiom, unbounded minimization, universal PR evaluator or general Turing/PR equivalence is assumed.
items.strategy:
Arithmetic closure is proved from the published initial-function/recursion definition. Addition and multiplication use a+0=a, a+S n=S(a+n), a·0=0 and a·S n=a·n+a. Define pred(0)=0, pred(S n)=n; truncated subtraction sub(a,0)=a and sub(a,S n)=pred(sub(a,n)); zero test z(0)=1,z(S n)=0. Equality is z(sub(a,b)+sub(b,a)), and a≤b is z(sub(a,b)). Boolean conjunction/product and complement 1−r give all finite tests; a case split is rg+(1−r)h. Bounded sums/products start at 0/1 and append one term. These are explicit primitive recursions. For a 0–1 predicate r, the least j<N satisfying r(j), or N if none, equals Σ_{j<N} Π_{i≤j}(1−r(i)); hence bounded minimization with any PR bound is PR. Exponentiation pow(b,0)=1,pow(b,S n)=b·pow(b,n). For d>0 the quotient of a by d is Σ_{q=1}^a [dq≤a], and the remainder is a−d·quotient; set both to zero for d=0. The natural-number division property follows directly by maximality and (q+1)d>a.

A fixed tuple of state registers can be stored by iterating P(u,v)=(u+v)^2+u. For fixed sum t its codes lie in [t²,t²+t], before the next interval [(t+1)²,...], and within it the u coordinate is distinct. Thus P is injective, and u,v≤P(u,v) for every pair. Its range test and inverse coordinates, returning zero off-range, are bounded searches u,v≤code. Therefore a simultaneous update of a fixed finite number of registers with PR coordinate updates reduces to one ordinary primitive recursion; no prior sequence-coding or loop theorem is used here. Updates may have arbitrarily large values; only the number of iterations must have a PR bound.

For s>0 its binary width is ell(s)=1+Σ_{j=1}^s [2^j≤s], and ell(0)=1. The jth left-to-right bit, for j<ell(s), is rem(quot(s,2^{ell(s)-1-j}),2); elsewhere use zero. Horner iteration v↦2v+b evaluates a payload. All are PR by the preceding formulas; powers of two increase and eventually exceed s by induction, so these formulas give the canonical binary word without a logarithm oracle.

The parser first checks s>0 and leading bit 1. Starting at position 1 it counts the consecutive 1s before the first 0; that 0 must exist, and its count k is the list length. Starting just after it, repeat k block parses. At a block start p, find the first following zero with bounded search below ell(s). Let m be its distance from p; require m≥1, the delimiter to exist, and m payload bits to fit after it. Require either m=1 or the first payload bit to be 1 (canonical numerals, with 0 permitted only as a one-bit payload). Horner evaluation gives that entry. Advance p by 2m+1. After exactly k blocks require p=ell(s). All position calculations are total, bounded-search failure sets a persistent invalid flag, and later iterations in invalid state do nothing. Counters, position, flag and the requested coordinate form finitely many registers; perform at most ell(s)+1 iterations per scan/block and at most ell(s)+1 block iterations. Nested bounded loops are compositions of the fixed-state recursion just proved. Thus validity, length and entries are PR, with an explicit final validity check resetting outputs to zero. The empty code 2 has k=0 and succeeds with no payload. Conversely deterministic delimiter lengths recover the unique original list, proving injectivity and correctness; no appeal to effective prefix coding is needed.

For construction keep a word as its value v together with its width L. Concatenating a width-M word of value w sends (v,L) to (v·2^M+w,L+M). Start the header at (2^{k+2}−2,k+2), which is precisely 1 1^k 0, including k=0. For an entry a of width m=ell(a), its block has width 2m+1 and value (2^m−1)·2^{m+1}+a. Iteratively concatenate these blocks; fixed-arity encoding is PR. For append or concatenation, use the validated input length(s) as the iteration bound, read each entry and add a block under the enlarged header. Default invalid inputs to the empty code 2. These definitions give PR operations and their intended effect by induction on the number of copied entries.

A numerical recursion that needs previous entries stores the entire current list code as its one state. If its initial value and next-value map are PR, combine next-value computation with the PR append operation, then invoke ordinary parameter recursion. Reading the last coordinate returns the requested output. This proves the needed history/course-of-values closure without a universal PR evaluation claim. For syntax operations every fixed-signature scanning instruction and each specified finite certificate transition is a combination of these arithmetic, list, case and iteration operations; the existing syntax lemma must still state its own bounds and correctness invariants.

items.title: Q calculates numerals and finite bounded cases
items.statement: Q decides each true or false closed arithmetic atomic formula; for every external n it proves x≤n→(x=0∨…∨x=n) and x≤n∨n+1≤x. It decides every closed bounded formula. These are metatheoretic schemes, not induction in Q.
items.strategy: External induction on n using predecessor axiom and successor injectivity proves the two order schemes for left-addend witnesses. Reduce closed terms using addition/multiplication recursion; use finite disjunction expansion for bounded quantifiers and Boolean induction, including zero bounds.

items.title: Beta coding and arithmetic sequence witnesses
items.statement: For β(b,c,i)=the remainder of b modulo 1+(i+1)c, every finite natural-number sequence has a β-code. Remainder and β admit numeralwise unique-value representations in Q. PA proves existence of codes for finite sequences and extension by one further coordinate.
items.strategy: Prove division by positive d by induction; prove Bezout by the Euclidean descent and the finite CRT by combining two congruences with Bezout coefficients (all these elementary arithmetic arguments are included here, not silent number-theory imports). Given a0,…,an choose j>max(n+1,a0,…,an) and c=j!: moduli 1+(i+1)c are pairwise coprime. A common prime divisor would divide (i-k)c, hence i-k, hence c, contradicting divisor of 1+(i+1)c. CRT supplies b. For Q use a remainder graph with bounded q,r and the finite numeral case lemma; for PA formalize division, Euclid and finite CRT by induction, permitting a new c when a coordinate is appended.

items.title: Numeralwise representation and arithmetic complexity
items.statement: F represents total f in Q when for every external tuple n, Q proves ∀y(F(n,y)↔y=f(n)). A relation is numeralwise expressed when Q proves each true numeral instance and negates each false one. Bounded arithmetic formulas quantify only below arithmetic terms; arithmetic Σ1 formulas are existential closures of bounded formulas, up to the explicitly stated base-theory equivalence.
items.strategy: Separate unique output at standard numeral inputs from the stronger PA theorem ∀x∃!y F(x,y); separate arithmetic bounded quantifiers from set-theoretic Δ0.

items.title: Primitive-recursive functions are representable in Q
items.statement: Every primitive-recursive function has a numeralwise unique-value representing formula in Q, and every primitive-recursive relation has positive and negative numeral proofs. The constructions can be chosen with PA-provable totality, uniqueness, and Σ1 graph definitions.
items.strategy: Induct on the construction of f. Base graphs are arithmetic equations; composition existentially binds intermediate values. For recursion use β-coded histories. Strengthen intermediate graphs by choosing the least candidate output so that agreement with a numeral forces any output to equal it even for nonnumeral inputs; finite order cases prove this property in Q. Require initial value, all successor equations through t, and final value at t (correct the displayed variable errors in Moschovakis 4B.12). External induction through a numeral t proves existence and unique final output. PA proves history existence by induction and the β-extension lemma; collecting finitely many witnesses gives Σ1 closure under bounded universal quantification. For f(0,x)=g(x), f(St,x)=h(t,f(t,x),x), use ∃b,c[∃u(G(x,u)∧B(b,c,0,u)) ∧ ∀i<t ∃u,v(B(b,c,i,u)∧B(b,c,Si,v)∧H(i,u,x,v)) ∧ B(b,c,t,y)], with G,H and B replaced by least-output-strengthened graphs. At each external numeral stage, the strengthened B graph forces every occurrence of a coordinate to agree with its computed numeral. The initial and successor clauses then force the terminal coordinate. The PA totality proof uses internally unique β values. For each external numeral r, the finite order cases prove uniformly in x that F*(x,r) implies every F*(x,y) has y=r: below r use the least-output clause at r, above r use the least-output clause at y, and equality is immediate. Thus no functionality of an arbitrary nonstandard history code is assumed. With numeral recursion input t, instantiate each of the finitely many successor clauses: G fixes the initial numeral; strengthened B transfers that value between occurrences; H fixes the next numeral; repeat through t, including t=0. Numeral beta codes give existence. The arithmetic complexity assertion uses PA equivalence explicitly: PA proves totality and uniqueness of each raw graph by the construction induction, hence proves it equivalent to its least-output strengthening. PA also proves its negation equivalent to existence of a different output. Starting with bounded beta graphs, replace earlier graphs and their negations by these positive existential forms and collect the finitely many witnesses under each bounded universal quantifier. This yields PA-provably equivalent syntactic Sigma1 formulas while retaining the strengthened graphs for Q numeral representation. The review obligation is discharged in research/phase-2-catchup-24-alpha-g-recheck.md; PA equivalence is not claimed to be Q equivalence.

items.title: Primitive-recursive syntax and certified proof checking
items.statement: Term/formula recognition, free-variable and free-for tests, capture-free substitution, numeral formation, negation, and checking a certified derivation are primitive recursive for the fixed encoding.
items.strategy: Scan decoded words with bounded stacks and bounded truth tables for tautology instances; calculate formula data in increasing syntax size, retaining finite histories. Rename bound variables above the largest index in the input before substitution. Check all six logical schemes and all three rules, including the existential-elimination eigenvariable restriction. Check every premise index is earlier; axiom certificates are checked by E, not by deciding ∃w E(a,w). Invalid inputs return 0/false. Prove all scanning loops bounded by numerical input or explicitly constructed primitive-recursive bounds. The local sentinel-code lemma supplies all numerical primitives, fixed-state iteration and history-list updates; no A609 theorem is assumed.

items.title: Interpretations with proof-translation data
items.statement: An interpretation of a sentence theory S in T specifies a definable nonempty domain D, an equivalence E on D, E-invariant relations, and E-invariant functional graphs total and single-valued modulo E on D. T proves these obligations and every translated S axiom. Translate terms by domain-valued witnesses, commute with Boolean operations, and relativize quantifiers to D. The proof translation of an open formula phi is G_FV(phi) -> phi^I, with G_V the conjunction of D(v) for v in V; sentences retain phi^I. Effective data supplies certificates effectively; formalized data additionally supplies a PA-verifiable primitive-recursive map on certified proofs.
items.strategy: Use one target domain variable per source variable and fresh auxiliary variables. Interpretation formulas have only designated free variables; parameters are fixed target constants. Define V_x(z):=D(z) and E(x,z). For a function application existentially bind argument values and conjoin its graph and D(z); nullary graphs cover constants. Translate atomic relations and equality through existential term values. Commute with negation and conjunction; translate exists x phi as exists x(D(x) and phi^I), expanding universal quantification through primitive syntax. The empty guard is a provable Boolean tautology. Interpretation data requires nonemptiness, E-equivalence, congruence, graph totality/uniqueness and translated sentence axioms, not logical theorem preservation. The next lemma proves substitution and all six axiom and three rule cases with free-variable guards. Identity equality on a definable subdomain is a special case. No quotient representatives or AC are needed. Effectiveness alone does not imply a base-verifiable primitive-recursive proof map.

items.title: Interpretation transports derivations and inconsistency
items.statement: For every S-derivation of a formula phi, the interpretation constructs a T-derivation of G_FV(phi) -> phi^I. For sentences this gives a T-derivation of phi^I; a source contradiction gives a T-contradiction. Thus external Con(T) implies Con(S). Effective certificate data makes the translation effective. If a base B verifies a total map from S-contradiction certificates to T-contradiction certificates, B proves Con(T) -> Con(S).
items.strategy:
Work in ZF with the fixed six-scheme/three-rule calculus. This local syntactic adaptation preserves sentence-consistency transport without semantic completeness or assuming logical theorem preservation as data. Use the published derived quantifier rules and open-discharge freshness clause, then assemble finite annotated proof blocks.

### Interpretation data and local structural inductions

Use one domain variable for each source variable, a domain formula D, an
equivalence E on D, relations invariant under E on D, and function graphs
total and single-valued modulo E on D and invariant under equivalent inputs.
T proves these obligations and the translations of the source sentence
axioms. These are data, not an assumption of logical theorem preservation.
Choose auxiliary variables fresh from the finite expressions being handled.

Define the term-value relation V_t(z) with output restricted to D:
for a variable x use D(z) and E(x,z); for a function application existentially
quantify the argument values and use its graph. The nullary case is the
constant graph. Translate atomic relations/equalities by existentially
quantifying their term values and applying the interpreted relation/E.
Commute with negation/conjunction and translate existential quantification
as exists x (D(x) and phi^I). All variables other than the designated domain
variables in the interpretation formulas must be bound or fixed constants.

Under the guard on the free input variables, induction on t proves existence
of a value, uniqueness modulo E, and invariance under E-equivalent inputs.
The variable case uses reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity of E on D. At a
function node, finitely many argument witnesses come from the induction;
totality supplies the output, and argument congruence plus graph uniqueness
compares any two outputs. Existence uses only finitely many existential
introductions/eliminations, not an infinite choice function.

Induction on formulas then proves invariance under E-equivalent free-variable
assignments: atomic cases use those value comparisons and relation congruence;
negation and conjunction use propositional rules; an existential witness
can be retained when changing the other free variables, so both directions
follow by existential monotonicity and fresh-variable elimination.

The simultaneous term/formula substitution induction gives, for free-for t,
under the guard on FV(phi) minus x together with FV(t),

    (phi[t/x])^I <-> exists z (V_t(z) and phi^I[z/x]).

Here z is fresh. Atomic cases substitute the value relations recursively.
For conjunction, two values can be identified modulo E and formula
invariance transports both conjuncts to one witness. For negation, values
exist and every value gives the same truth value by invariance; hence
negating the existential value formula equals existence of a value satisfying
the negated formula. This is the necessary uniqueness step; existential
quantification does not simply commute with negation. For quantifiers,
rename their binders away from t,z and use existential monotonicity and
fresh-variable elimination to commute the independent witnesses. If x is
absent, the same equivalence follows by value existence. Every operation
uses the published syntactic rules, not semantic completeness.

### Guard removal and six axiom cases

Let G_V be the conjunction of D(v) for the finite free-variable set V.
If T proves G_(V union {x}) -> A and x is absent from A and G_V, Boolean
commutation gives D(x) -> (G_V -> A). Restricted existential elimination
gives (exists x D(x)) -> (G_V -> A). Apply domain nonemptiness to remove
that guard. Repeating this removes every surplus free-variable guard.
An empty guard is a fixed provable Boolean tautology.

1. Boolean tautologies remain tautologies after substituting translated
   formulas for their propositional atoms; add the guard by weakening.
2. Universal instantiation: under the needed input guard, obtain a value
   of t. The relativized universal premise gives phi^I at that value.
   The substitution equivalence gives the translated conclusion. Remove
   surplus guards; if x never occurs in phi this is simply A -> A.
3. Distribution: from forall x(D(x) -> (A -> B)) and A, infer
   forall x(D(x) -> B), since x is absent from A. This is the target
   distribution axiom after Boolean rearrangement and generalization.
4. Existential introduction: substitution provides a value of t with
   phi^I at that value, hence exists x(D(x) and phi^I). Again remove
   any guard not in the actual source axiom's free-variable set.
5. Reflexivity: the term has a value; E is reflexive on its values, so
   the interpreted t=t follows. A variable outside D is never asserted
   E-reflexive without its free-variable guard.
6. Equality substitution: choose values of s and t. Interpreted equality
   makes them E-equivalent. Formula invariance transfers the substituted
   formula between them; the substitution equivalences recover the exact
   two interpreted formulas. Discharge the interpreted equality premise
   and remove surplus guards. All witnesses are fresh.

These finite derivations can be written with temporary open assumptions
only using variables absent from those assumptions for generalization or
existential elimination. The published open-discharge clause then applies.
Equivalently all steps can be expressed as Boolean implication templates.

### Three rule cases and consistency

Maintain T proves G_FV(phi) -> phi^I for every source line phi.
Source sentence assumptions use their supplied target proofs directly.

- MP: enlarge both premise guards to their finite union, apply MP to the
  translated formulas, then remove variables absent from the conclusion.
- Generalization in x: let G omit x. From the transformed premise obtain
  G -> (D(x) -> phi^I), adding a vacuous D(x) guard if necessary.
  Generalize x and use distribution, since x is absent from G, to get
  G -> forall x(D(x) -> phi^I). Expanding the primitive syntax and using the published quantified
  double-negation rule gives the relativized universal conclusion.
- Restricted existential elimination: x is absent from psi. Rewrite the
  transformed implication as (D(x) and phi^I) -> (G -> psi^I), where G
  contains the remaining free-variable guards and omits x. Eliminate x,
  which is absent from G -> psi^I, then commute the implication to obtain
  G -> ((exists x(D(x) and phi^I)) -> psi^I). Remove surplus guards.

The fixed source contradiction is exists v0 not(v0=v0). Its translation
is refutable in T by guarded E-reflexivity and the term-value argument.
It has no free variables, so a translated source contradiction proof gives
its unguarded translation; explosion then gives T's fixed contradiction.
This proves external consistency transport without changing the calculus.

For each finite source proof only finitely many interpretation-obligation
and source-axiom certificates are needed; finite selection and concatenation
are justified in ZF by the read finite-support lemma. Effective certificate
data gives an effective translation through these explicit templates.
Do not infer a PA-verifiable primitive-recursive map merely from that fact.
The formalized claim retains its separate hypothesis that B verifies a total
map from S-contradiction certificates to T-contradiction certificates; quantify
over codes and contrapose that verified implication inside B.

items.title: The standard certified provability predicate
items.statement: Prf_T(p,a) is the chosen arithmetic representation of certified T-proof checking (proof code first); Prov_T(a):=∃p Prf_T(p,a). Con(T):=¬Prov_T(code(⊥)), for the fixed contradictory sentence of the appropriate signature. This arithmetical formula differs from the external assertion that T has no finite proof of contradiction.
items.strategy: Retain the Q-numeralwise proof-checking representation from the preceding theorem and fix its PA-provably equivalent syntactic Sigma1 form by coded computations, together with the finite PA proofs of that equivalence. Here Sigma1 for the chosen predicate means PA-Sigma1 as explicitly allowed in def-numeralwise-representability-and-arithmetic-sigma-one. State PA-verifiable transformations; never infer Q equivalence from PA equivalence. For arithmetic use 0=1 interchangeably with the fixed bottom only after exhibiting proof translations. Arbitrary numeralwise correct predicates are not automatically eligible for second incompleteness.

items.title: The syntactic diagonal lemma
items.statement: For every formula ψ(v) of an effective signature extending arithmetic and T extending Q, there is a sentence θ with Q (in that signature) proving θ↔ψ(code θ). The construction is effective; no consistency or soundness assumption is required.
items.strategy: Let d(e) code substitution of numeral e into the designated variable of formula e. Represent d by D. Choose fresh y and let η(x)=∃y(D(x,y)∧ψ(y)), θ=η(code η). The numeralwise uniqueness theorem identifies its sole output as code θ; existential introduction and elimination give both implications. Expand all abbreviations and avoid treating d as an unlicensed function symbol.

items.title: Gödel sentence with separated consistency assumptions
items.statement: For an effective T extending Q, choose G↔¬Prov_T(code G). If T is consistent, T does not prove G and G is true in standard arithmetic. If T is ω-consistent (in particular if sound), T does not prove ¬G.
items.strategy: A proof of G gives a positive numeral proof of its proof code and hence Prov G, contradicting G. Under consistency each standard proof-code instance is refutable in Q. A proof of ¬G would prove existence of such a proof code while refuting each numeral instance, violating ω-consistency. State ω-consistency in the contract; do not claim consistency alone rules out ¬G.

items.title: Rosser incompleteness from consistency
items.statement: Every consistent effective theory extending Q is incomplete. The result also holds for a theory with an effective interpretation of Q, using proof predicates for translated sentences.
items.strategy: Choose R↔∀p(Prf_T(p,code R)→∃q≤p Prf_T(q,code ¬R)). If T proves R with code m, consistency and finite negative numeral checking refute every candidate q≤m, hence refute R. If T proves ¬R with code n, consistency rules out each proof code p≤n; for p>n the code n witnesses the consequent. The two bounded cases give a Q proof of R, contradiction. For interpretations use translated Proof/Refute predicates, keeping R itself an arithmetic sentence before translation.

items.title: PA verifies proof certificates for bounded arithmetic truth
items.statement: For each fixed bounded arithmetic formula δ(x), PA proves that δ(x) yields a certified Q-proof of δ(numeral x), and ¬δ(x) yields a certified Q-proof of its negation. Therefore for each fixed Σ1 sentence σ, PA proves σ→Prov_Q(code σ).
items.strategy: Build primitive-recursive proof constructors simultaneously for true and false cases. Atomic term evaluation uses recursive numeral addition and multiplication proofs; inequality uses successor injectivity. Boolean constructors splice proofs and tautologies. Bounded existential truth uses the least successful witness and introduction; bounded universal truth concatenates proofs for every value and uses the finite case theorem; their false cases reverse these operations. PA induction on the numerical bound verifies the list construction and premise indices. Fixed formula complexity is external; numerical induction is internal. For Σ1 append existential introductions to the bounded witness proof. This supplies the work omitted by Avigad rather than postulating derivability conditions. The concluding Q-certificate assertion applies to a syntactic Sigma1 sentence (existential closure of a bounded formula). For a formula only PA-provably equivalent to that sentence, first obtain the Q-proof of the syntactic form, then embed it into the target extending PA and append the fixed PA equivalence proof there; do not claim a Q-proof of the equivalent formula.

items.title: Derivability conditions for the chosen proof predicate
items.statement: For the standard certified predicate of an effective T extending PA (or an effective interpreted PA copy), D1: T⊢φ implies T⊢Prov_T(code φ); D2: T proves Prov_T(code(φ→ψ))→(Prov_T(code φ)→Prov_T(code ψ)); D3: T proves Prov_T(code φ)→Prov_T(code Prov_T(code φ)).
items.strategy: D1 inserts the actual finite proof certificate and a numeral verification. D2 uses the PA-verifiable primitive-recursive operation concatenating two proofs, shifting references and appending MP. For D3 write chi=Prov_T(code phi), and use the fixed PA proof chi iff sigma, with sigma syntactic Sigma1. PA proves sigma implies Prov_Q(code sigma) by the preceding certificate lemma. Embed those Q certificates into T and append the fixed T-proof of sigma implies chi; the PA-verifiable concatenation operation therefore gives sigma implies Prov_T(code chi). Combining with chi implies sigma proves D3. No Q proof of chi iff sigma is asserted or needed. For interpreted arithmetic explicitly transport these proof constructors and require the PA interpretation/axiom-proof map to be verifiable there. Do not apply to an arbitrary nonstandard presentation merely correct on standard numerals.

items.title: Löb theorem
items.statement: For T extending Q, or with an effective interpreted Q copy supporting the diagonal construction, with a standard provability predicate satisfying D1–D3, if T proves Prov_T(code φ)→φ, then T proves φ.
items.strategy: Take θ↔(Prov θ→φ). D1 and D2 give Prov θ→Prov(Prov θ→φ); D3 and D2 give Prov θ→Prov φ. The assumed reflection instance gives Prov θ→φ, hence θ. D1 gives Prov θ, then φ. This proof precedes second incompleteness and uses no consistency hypothesis.

items.title: Second incompleteness for standard provability
items.statement: If T is consistent and satisfies the preceding arithmetic and derivability hypotheses (including the interpreted version), T does not prove its displayed Con(T). The theorem requires the chosen proof predicate and verified arithmetic interpretation, not mere numeralwise correctness.
items.strategy: Con(T) is equivalent in T to Prov_T(code ⊥)→⊥; Löb would turn its provability into a proof of ⊥. The particular axiom presentation and predicate are part of the theorem.

items.title: Arithmetic truth is not arithmetically definable
items.statement: No arithmetic formula defines the set of codes of all sentences true in the standard natural-number structure. More generally no consistent extension of Q has a formula Tr satisfying all its own-language T-biconditionals.
items.strategy: For a purported Tr, diagonalize ¬Tr. In standard arithmetic soundness of Q makes the fixed-point biconditional true, contradicting the truth-definition biconditional. For a consistent theory the two proved biconditionals already contradict each other. Verify the standard arithmetic structure satisfies the seven Q axioms; this makes no appeal to its own truth predicate.

items.title: Explicit definitions are conservative
items.statement: Adding relation symbols by explicit defining formulas, and functions by formulas T proves uniquely total, is conservative over T in its original language. It is equiconsistent with T.
items.strategy: Use the full target domain D(x):=x=x and actual equality E(x,y):=x=y. Interpret each old symbol by itself and each new symbol by its defining old-language relation or uniquely total graph. Eliminate graph occurrences with fresh variables. Under this interpretation every free-variable guard is a theorem. For each old term t prove V_t(z) iff z=t by structural induction; equality substitution and unique totality discharge the witnesses. Induction on old formulas then proves phi^I iff phi using the published quantifier monotonicity and renaming rules. Thus identity on the old language means provable equivalence, not literal equality of the witness-expanded syntax. Translate a proof of an old sentence through the guarded interpretation lemma, remove its vacuous guard and use this equivalence to obtain the original sentence in T. The defining axioms translate to theorems by the same graph equations and their stipulated existence/uniqueness proofs. Fixed contradiction gives one consistency direction; inclusion of T gives the converse. Only finitely many definition certificates occur in a finite proof, so finite proof assembly suffices in ZF; no AC or completeness is used.

items.title: ZF has an effective standard arithmetic interpretation
items.statement: ZF and ZFC have effective axiom presentations and an interpretation of PA on ω with von Neumann zero/successor and recursively defined addition/multiplication. Their standard proof predicates satisfy the preceding formalization requirements.
items.strategy: Use the published coded ZF schema serialization exactly, including implication-only Power Set and von Neumann Infinity. Syntactic parsing gives a primitive-recursive schema enumerator/certificates. Define addition and multiplication by recursion on ω and verify seven Q axioms. Separation forms the induction set for every translated formula, and ω induction proves the PA induction schema. Supply uniform formula-to-schema-instance and proof translations. AC is only an additional encoded sentence for ZFC, not needed to interpret PA. Verify the interpreted primitive-recursive proof constructors in PA on ω, then apply the derivability-conditions theorem; this supplies second incompleteness for ZF, ZFC and their finite effective extensions.

items.title: Models and consistency for countable theories
items.statement: In external ZF, an explicitly countable sentence theory is consistent iff it has a nonempty set model, and iff it has an at most countable set model. For an effective presentation the external consistency assertion agrees with truth in standard ω of its certified Con formula. No transitivity or external well-foundedness follows.
items.strategy: First reduce to the sublanguage consisting of symbols occurring in the explicitly countable theory: code each occurrence by its theory-sentence index and token position, and assign each occurring symbol its least occurrence code. This gives an explicit injection into omega without countable choice, including the empty-theory case. Consistency is preserved on restriction because any proof in the smaller signature is also a proof in the original signature. Apply published countable completeness in this explicitly countable sublanguage. Choose one element of the nonempty model, interpret every unused constant and function by that element (constant functions of the prescribed arities), and every unused relation by the empty relation. Reduct invariance of satisfaction shows the expansion satisfies the original theory and has the same at most countable carrier. Conversely apply published soundness. Numerical certification equivalence converts each actual finite derivation for an effective presentation. The Henkin quotient relation need not be actual membership and internal naturals need not be standard.

items.title: Transitive models and finite-fragment transfer data
items.statement: TM(Γ) means a nonempty transitive set M with the real restricted membership relation satisfies Γ; CTM adds an injection M→ω. A fragment transfer specifies, for each finite target fragment Δ, a finite source fragment Γ and a theorem converting each suitable TM/CTM of Γ into a set model of Δ. Countability is external to the model.
items.strategy: Define transitive explicitly by ∀x∈M∀y∈x(y∈M). Fragment source, auxiliary axioms, parameter restrictions and metatheory are part of the data. The assertion Γ⊂ZF is syntactic. Do not quantify a universe truth predicate or assume a full CTM from consistency.

items.title: Transitive ZF models have standard arithmetic and proof codes
items.statement: A transitive set model of ZF has the real ω, natural arithmetic and all finite natural-number syntax/proof codes. For each fixed effective arithmetic predicate its truth on those codes agrees with the ambient universe. If it models ZFC, it also satisfies the standard Con(ZFC).
items.strategy: External induction fixes every finite ordinal. Its internal ω is a transitive ordinal with only zero/successor elements, no largest element, and is nonzero: this excludes an extra ordinal ≥real ω and proves equality. Arithmetic recursion agrees by uniqueness; formula induction then gives arithmetic absoluteness since all quantifiers range over the same ω. Soundness in the ambient universe gives absence of an actual ZFC proof of contradiction, then arithmetic absoluteness transfers the Con sentence inside M.

items.title: The transitive-model consistency-strength gap
items.statement: Let S=ZFC+Con(ZFC). Assuming externally Con(S), ZFC does not prove Con(ZFC)→TM(ZFC). Moreover S+¬TM(ZFC) is consistent and has a set model. Thus consistency is not a valid replacement for a transitive-model hypothesis.
items.strategy: ZF proves TM(ZFC)→Con(S): a transitive ZFC model satisfies Con(ZFC) by proof-code correctness, hence is a model of S, and soundness applies. If S proved TM(ZFC), it would prove Con(S), contrary to second incompleteness for S. Deduction gives consistency of S+¬TM(ZFC), and countable completeness gives the relative countermodel. State the stronger external hypothesis Con(S) explicitly; do not claim Con(ZFC) alone proves this countermodel exists.

items.title: Finite-fragment model transfer proves relative consistency
items.statement: Let T extend enough ZF to formalize set-model soundness and U be an explicitly countable sentence theory. Suppose for every external finite Δ⊂U there is finite Γ and T-proofs of existence of a suitable TM/CTM of Γ and of its conversion to a set model of Δ. Then external Con(T) implies Con(U).
items.strategy: Assume an actual U-refutation p; extract its finite axiom support Δ. The two stipulated T-proofs imply a set model of Δ exists. Formal soundness for the fixed proof p gives its impossibility in T, so T is inconsistent. Only this finite support is needed. This is a metatheorem/scheme; it is not the internal uniform sentence ∀finite Δ∃Γ without further proof generation. Reflection is later supplied by SET-5, not assumed as a forward dependency here.

items.title: Formal consistency transfer from a verified reduction
items.statement: If an arithmetic base B verifies a total code map r and ∀p(Prf_U(p,⊥)→Prf_T(r(p),⊥)), then B proves Con(T)→Con(U). For finite-fragment/reflection applications, the maps extracting support, producing source fragments, and compiling reflection/transfer/soundness proofs must be supplied and verified to obtain such r.
items.strategy: Quantify over p, apply the correctness implication, and use Con(T) to exclude its consequent. Account separately for totality of r in B. Package the earlier finite-fragment argument into r only when its source/target axiom certificate maps and schema-proof constructors have actually been checked in B. No claim that a bare semantic CTM theorem automatically supplies these maps.

items.statement: If PA is consistent then PA+¬Con(PA) is consistent and has a model; every such model has a nonstandard code it regards as a PA-refutation.
items.strategy: If the extension were inconsistent deduction would give PA⊢Con(PA), contrary to G2. Each standard alleged proof fails its finite check; hence the model witness is nonstandard. Do not call the model externally sound.

items.title: The Lévy hierarchy and absoluteness
items.statement: Set-theoretic Δ0 formulas use bounded membership quantifiers only. Define Σ0=Π0=Δ0, then Σ(n+1)/Π(n+1) by existential/universal unbounded quantification over the opposite level, positive Boolean combinations and bounded quantification; allow equivalent formulas only over a named theory such as ZF. Δn means both a Σn and Πn definition modulo that theory. Absoluteness for M⊆N means agreement on all parameter tuples in M.
items.strategy: Give the simultaneous syntactic closure clauses, duality under negation and constants for empty Boolean cases. Arithmetic Σ1 is a different hierarchy. For definable classes relativization is a separate formula for each external formula, not a uniform truth predicate.

items.title: Bounded formulas are absolute for transitive sets
items.statement: If M⊆N are nonempty transitive sets, every Δ0 formula is absolute between them for parameters in M. The same holds schematically for definable transitive classes. No set-theoretic axioms need hold inside M or N.
items.strategy: Atomic membership/equality are actual relations; negation and conjunction preserve agreement. A quantifier bounded by a∈M ranges over exactly the same actual elements in both structures because M is transitive. Prove both directions, with parameter restriction to the smaller structure.

items.title: Absolute basic set operations and relations
items.statement: Graphs for empty set, subset, pairing, singleton, union, intersection (empty intersection convention ∅), difference, ordered pairs, products, relation domain/range, functionhood, evaluation and injection are Δ0 after explicit bounded expansions. Their values agree whenever present in the smaller transitive structure.
items.strategy: Write bounded graph formulas; bind possible pair coordinates inside double unions of a supplied pair/set. Eliminate union abbreviations through bounded graph formulas. Distinguish graph absoluteness from existence/closure of the operation inside an arbitrary transitive set; no Power Set absoluteness claim.

items.title: Ordinals and omega in transitive models
items.statement: In ambient ZF, ordinalhood is absolute for transitive sets containing the parameter. Transitive models of ZF have exactly the actual ω and correct finite ordinals. A transitive model’s ordinals form an initial segment of the ambient ordinals.
items.strategy: Use the bounded formula transitive and membership-linear; ambient Foundation makes it a well-order. Characterize ω as a NONZERO limit ordinal every element of which is zero or a successor. Include nonzero explicitly (the Freiburg displayed shorthand otherwise also accepts 0). Transitivity and external induction identify finite ordinals and rule out extra elements.

items.title: Ranks agree and hierarchy membership is absolute
items.statement: If M⊆N are transitive models of ZF and x∈M, rank^M(x)=rank^N(x). For α∈Ord∩M, (V_α)^M=M∩(V_α)^N. This does not assert equality of internal power sets or of the two hierarchy-stage sets.
items.strategy: External membership induction on x: M contains every member y of x; the two rank recursions have identical predecessor values and ordinal suprema. Thus ranks agree. Apply the rank characterization of x∈V_α in both models, for x∈M. Both models must supply the internal rank recursion; graph absoluteness alone does not supply its existence.

items.title: Sigma-one formulas admit existential bounded matrices
items.statement: Over ZF, each Σ1 formula in the bounded-closure convention is equivalent to an existential block followed by a Δ0 matrix.
items.strategy: Induct over construction. Combine existential witnesses into finite tuples; Boolean disjunction uses a finite tag and conjunction pairs witnesses. For bounded ∀x∈a∃y δ, Collection gives a witness set b; rewrite as ∃b∀x∈a∃y∈b δ. Matrix remains bounded. Bounded existential is immediate. Record use of Collection/Replacement and do not assert this equivalence over every weak theory.

items.title: Sigma-one truth goes upward
items.statement: For transitive M⊆N, a formula literally ∃x1…∃xk δ with Δ0 matrix transfers truth from M to N; its Π1 dual transfers downward. For ZF-equivalent Σ1/Π1 formulas require both structures to satisfy ZF (or the exact equivalence axioms).
items.strategy: Retain the witnesses in M⊆N and apply Δ0 agreement to the tuple; contrapose for Π1. The normal-form dependency is used only for the bounded-closure convention and carries its stated axiom requirement.

items.title: A finite witness criterion for reflection
items.statement: For a finite subformula-closed family Φ and nonempty C⊆D with actual membership, all Φ formulas agree between C,D iff every existential subformula true in D with parameters in C has a witness in C satisfying its matrix in D. Class forms are schemes.
items.strategy: Induct on each formula; atomic relations restrict automatically, Boolean cases preserve equivalence, and the existential case uses precisely the stated witness condition. For necessity first transfer the existential, select its C witness, then transfer the matrix. No full elementary submodel of V is postulated.

items.title: Least witness ranks give choice-free bounds
items.statement: For each fixed finite formula family and each ordinal α, a definable ordinal b(α)>α bounds ranks of witnesses for all true existential instances whose parameters lie in V_α. A version applies to any definable increasing continuous exhaustive hierarchy of sets.
items.strategy: For each parameter tuple minimize a witness rank (or first hierarchy level containing a witness), using 0 when no witness exists. Replacement collects the ordinal values over the set of finite parameter tuples; take a successor bound. Choose bounds rather than witnesses, so no AC. Each formula is fixed externally; no truth predicate for all formulas is invoked.

items.title: Montague–Lévy reflection for a finite formula family
items.statement: In ZF, for each fixed finite family Φ of formulas and every ordinal α there is β>α such that Φ is absolute between V_β and V, on all tuples from V_β. More generally replace V_γ by an increasing continuous definable hierarchy W_γ exhausting a definable class W.
items.strategy: Close Φ under subformulas, start above α, iterate the definable bound b along ω, and let β be the supremum. Any finite tuple in the union lies at one stage, whose required witnesses lie in the next stage. Continuity and the finite witness criterion give reflection. Specify Infinity/Replacement for the sequence, Union for its supremum, Separation/Replacement for rank bounds, Power Set for V stages and Foundation for exhaustion. No AC or full truth predicate.

items.title: Transitive models of fixed finite axiom fragments
items.statement: For every fixed external finite Γ⊂ZF, ZF proves that some V_β satisfies Γ, with β above any specified ordinal bound. In ZFC the analogous scheme holds for finite Γ⊂ZFC. This is not a single theorem asserting a model of every internally coded finite fragment.
items.strategy: Reflect the finitely many axiom formulas and conjoin their theorems in the ambient theory. Use a bound above ω when infinite models are needed. No circular use of consistency and no simultaneous all-formula reflection. The ZF-fragment branch uses no AC. In the ZFC-fragment branch, the ambient AC sentence from def-axiom-of-choice is used exactly when it occurs among the reflected axioms; the reflection construction itself remains choice-free. This branch is a ZFC theorem scheme, not a ZF assertion that the Choice axiom holds.

items.title: Collapse of elementary membership submodels
items.statement: Let M be a set, (M,∈) satisfy Extensionality, and X≺(M,∈). In ambient ZF the restricted membership on X is well-founded and extensional, so X has a unique transitive collapse Xbar; the inverse collapse is an elementary embedding Xbar→M.
items.strategy: Foundation gives external well-foundedness on every subset X, not merely internal Foundation in an arbitrary (M,E). If a≠b in X, Extensionality in M and elementarity supply a distinguishing member in X, proving restricted extensionality. Mostowski gives the set collapse and isomorphism invariance transfers formulas. Countability is preserved by the bijection.

items.title: What the collapse fixes
items.statement: For a collapse π:X→Xbar of actual membership, π is the identity on every transitive subset A⊆X. For α∈X an actual ordinal, π(α) is the order type of X∩α; if X∩α is transitive it equals that intersection.
items.strategy: Membership induction fixes each a∈A because all its predecessors are in A. Restrict the collapse equation to the well-ordered set X∩α; its range is an ordinal and the restriction is its order isomorphism. Do not replace X∩α by α unless α⊆X.

items.title: Countable elementary submodels and their collapses
items.statement: In ZFC an infinite set membership structure M satisfying Extensionality has, for every at most countable A⊆M, a countable elementary submodel X containing A, and X has a countable transitive collapse.
items.strategy: Apply downward LS with κ=aleph0 and countable membership language, then the collapse theorem. AC is used to select the Skolem witnesses/enumerations as in the supplier; the collapse itself is choice-free. If A∈M and the intention is to retain A as one parameter, use {A} rather than silently demanding A⊆X.

items.title: Countable transitive models of fixed finite fragments
items.statement: For every fixed finite Γ⊂ZFC, ZFC proves existence of a countable transitive model of Γ. The same construction under ambient AC works for fixed finite Γ⊂ZF.
items.strategy: Enlarge Γ by Extensionality, reflect above ω so V_β is infinite, take a countable elementary submodel, and collapse. Transfer Γ via the isomorphism. Neither internal Foundation alone nor arbitrary countable model existence replaces external well-foundedness.

items.title: Elementary chains and compatible collapses
items.statement: For a nonempty set-ordinal elementary chain of actual membership structures satisfying Extensionality, its union is an elementary extension of each stage and has a transitive collapse. The stage-to-union embeddings conjugate through their collapses to coherent elementary embeddings; these need not be literal subset inclusions between the transitive collapses.
items.strategy: Apply the published union theorem with the membership signature. For collapse maps πα and π define jα=π∘inclusion∘πα^{-1}; isomorphism invariance gives elementarity, and cancellation gives coherence. Do not assert that collapsing commutes with plain unions of the resulting carriers.

items.title: A countable elementary submodel need not be transitive
items.statement: False statement: every countable elementary submodel of a transitive set is transitive. In ZFC take θ with ω1∈V_θ, choose countable X≺V_θ containing ω1; then X is not transitive.
items.strategy: Hartogs supplies an uncountable ordinal ω1; choose θ large enough that V_θ is infinite and satisfies Extensionality. Downward LS supplies X with ω1 as a parameter. If X were transitive, ω1⊆X, contradicting countability. The collapse sends ω1 to the countable order type of X∩ω1; X∩ω1 need not be replaced by ω1.

sources.title: Geschke, Models of Set Theory
sources.locator: §4 Theorem 4.4 and Exercise 4.7 pp11–12, local counterexample

items.title: Transporting an elementary-chain map through collapse
items.statement: The formula jαβ=πβ∘inclusion∘πα^{-1} is the correct map between collapsed stages; equality with inclusion is an additional property. In ZFC, a countable elementary X containing the Hartogs ordinal of omega inside V_(kappa+omega) supplies a map moving its collapsed ordinal to kappa.
items.strategy: Check jβγ jαβ=jαγ by cancelling inverse maps. Compute its action on a named ordinal as the corresponding order-type embedding. Do not claim it is automatically a literal subset inclusion.

sources.title: Geschke, Models of Set Theory
